findings.title: GitHub user validation is bypassed when `Integration` record does not yet exist
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, when `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist` (lines 475-482), the view immediately returns `pipeline.next_step()`, which finishes the pipeline and calls `build_integration(state)` without ever comparing `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` against the user who installed the GitHub App. This happens whenever the `installation.created` webhook has not yet been processed (a race condition) or failed, or when an existing `Integration` record was deleted after uninstallation from Sentry while the GitHub App installation itself remains active on GitHub (as demonstrated by `test_github_installed_on_another_org` at line 365, where `sender` is never set at all and the test still succeeds). An attacker who knows or guesses a target's `installation_id` in this state can bind that GitHub installation to their own Sentry organization despite authenticating as a different GitHub user.

findings.title: Direct access to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` can raise `KeyError`
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is indexed directly without checking whether `"sender"` exists in `integration.metadata`. `build_integration` (line 376) only sets `integration["metadata"]["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, so any `Integration` record created outside the webhook flow (or before `sender` was recorded) will not have `"sender"` in `metadata`. If its `OrganizationIntegration` is removed and a user attempts to re-link the installation, this line will raise an unhandled `KeyError` (HTTP 500) instead of handling the missing sender gracefully.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests a missing GitHub installation
findings.body: In `test_installation_not_found`, the second request passes `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which does not match the pipeline signature (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`), and `self.init_path` is never called to initialize the pipeline with `self.installation_id`. As a result, `OAuthLoginView` fails early on the OAuth `state` mismatch check (line 412 of `integration.py`) and returns `"Invalid installation request."`, never reaching `GitHubInstallation` or `build_integration` where the mocked 404 from `/app/installations/{installation_id}` would be hit. The 404 handling in `build_integration` is therefore no longer exercised by this test.
